calls.head: Like for like: Dach vs. Klapka
calls.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending Dach’s line (Frederic, Dach and Howard) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Flames’ fourth line is Othmann, Castagna and Klapka.

calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Edmonton is the league’s best, but Calgary is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Flames take could cost them. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates more per 60 than the Flames’.

surprises.head: A shutout for Tristan Jarry
surprises.body: Jarry stopped all 24 shots, worth 2.0 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 15 starts.

story.head: Nothing gets past Jarry
paras: Early in the first, Ty Emberson and Brennan Othmann squared off, and Mathieu Joseph struck first for the Oilers. Dustin Wolf took over from Devin Cooley in net for Calgary to start the second. Mattias Ekholm made it 2-0 for the Oil early in the second. Kasperi Kapanen and Alex Formenton scored 21 seconds apart early in the third to stretch the lead to 4-0, and the Flames never had an answer.

The Oilers drove the play, outshooting the Flames 32-24, and the scoreboard caught up. Tristan Jarry turned aside all 24 shots for the Oilers. The Oilers improved to 9-2-2 and climbed into first in the Pacific, while the Flames fell to 5-7-0, sixth in the Pacific.
